liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Lost Sailor** (2 reviews): Reviewer finds the Lost Sailor into Saint of Circumstance sequence incredible; Reviewer considers the Lost Sailor into Saint of Circumstance the best recording they own [9][12]
- **The Other One** (2 reviews): Jazz drummer Billy Cobham sat in with the band during Drums leading into The Other One; Billy Cobham joined the drummers at the center of The Beast for Drums, Space and The Other One [5][15]
- **I've Been All Around This World** (1 review): Reviewer calls it their favorite Jerry song and loved seeing it performed live [11]

## Setlist highlights

- **New New Minglewood Vlues**: back after 181 archived shows (739 days); rare: 13 archived performances [17]
- **drums**: with Billy Cobham [17]
- **encore applause & tunig**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [17]

## The recordings

- **gd1980-10-30.139599.sbd.bershaw.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 29 songs; 216 min; rated 4.75/5 by 4 [1]
- **gd80-10-30.wise.larson.1954.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 28 songs; 198 min; rated 4/5 by 8 [2]
- **gd1980-10-30.fob.sonyecm280.wise.miller.101427.flac16**: source not stated; 27 songs; 200 min; rated 4.5/5 by 8 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer describes the recording as having beautiful sound, and an all-around excellent recording; Reviewer praises Jim Wise's audience recording as excellent [12][15]
- **gd1980-10-30.120537.nak70.gatto-jaeger.dusborne.flac16**: source not stated; 27 songs; 198 min; rated 2/5 by 2 [4]

## Around the show

- Guests: Billy Cobham [1]
- Stage talk about: John Scher [1]
- Reviewer's first Dead show, a week before turning 15; camped four days for tickets to this show and the 31st, skipping school [6]
- Reviewer scalped an orchestra seat for $80, a week's pay, and recalls Billy Cobham on drums [11]
- Reviewer thinks the band played with extra focus because they knew the run was being recorded for live albums [11]
- Reviewer attended four of the eight shows in this run and saw Billy Cobham play on The Other One [14]
- The recording is complete, beginning with John Scher's introduction before the acoustic set [1]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1980-10-30.139599.sbd.bershaw.flac16**: transferred by Alan Bershaw; source: Source: 10Ó 1/4 track SBD Feed Master Reels @ 7.5ips; [1]. Also: Soundboard direct recording, previously uncirculated, made in mono on two 10-inch quarter-track reels at 7.5 ips [1]
- **gd80-10-30.wise.larson.1954.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Jim Wise; source: Audience Recording: Sony ECM-280/D-5 [2]. Also: The Truckin' through Other One segment comes from the USA Network's Dead Ahead broadcast, absent from the shorter main film release [5]
- **gd1980-10-30.fob.sonyecm280.wise.miller.101427.flac16**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: (FOB) Sony ECM-280 -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/Maxell UDXLII-C90/Dolby B) [3]
- **gd1980-10-30.120537.nak70.gatto-jaeger.dusborne.flac16**: taped by Keith Gatto & Pete Jaeger; transferred by Michael Turi and dusborne; source: Loge Dead front center; Nak 700 > sony D-5> AMC> DAT> CDR> EAC> TLH> Flac; Recorded by Keith Gatto & Pete Jaeger; Extracted & flac encoded by Michael Turi;… [4]
